name: CHT (Compact Hist-Tree)
workload: SOSD benchmark equality lookups over 200M-key real-world datasets (amzn, face, osm, wiki), average lookup latency over 1M uniformly-random queries
claimed_speedup: CHT beats RMI by 1.1-1.8x, PGM-index by 1.7-2.5x, and RadixSpline by 1.2-2.7x in lookup latency; the compact (read-only) layout is 2-3x faster than the updatable Hist-Tree (HT) variant; also 3.7x-19x faster build times than RMI on face/wiki datasets
hardware: AWS c5.4xlarge EC2 instance, Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M CPU @ 3.0GHz, 26MB LLC
stars_or_usage: 9 stars; benchmarked against SOSD's tuned RMI/PGM/RadixSpline implementations
tradeoffs: Compact layout is build-once/read-only (no updates); the updatable HT variant exists but is 2-3x slower on lookups; author credited as Andrew Crotty (Brown University), repo implementation by Mihail Stoian
caveats: Numbers come from the CIDR 2021 paper (Crotty, 'Hist-Tree: Those Who Ignore It Are Doomed to Learn'), not from the repo's own README, which has no benchmark section; repo has had no commits since 2021
found_via: learnedsystems/SOSD .gitmodules -> competitors/CHT submodule (stoianmihail/CHT); paper located via Andrew Crotty's Brown CS publications page

name: TidesDB
workload: 8-thread benchmark, 16-byte keys / 100-byte values, 5M keys for random/sequential seeks and range queries, 650K unique keys for Zipfian-distributed seeks (TidesDB v6.1.0 vs RocksDB v10.7.5, benchtool)
claimed_speedup: Random seeks 4.17x faster (3.73M vs 893K ops/sec); sequential seeks 4.74x faster (8.87M vs 1.87M ops/sec); Zipfian seeks 5.25x faster (3.56M vs 679K ops/sec); small (100-key) range queries 2.41x faster; large (1000-key) range queries 1.11x faster
hardware: Intel Core i7-11700K (8 cores/16 threads @ 4.9GHz), 48GB DDR4, WD 500GB SATA SSD, Ubuntu 23.04 x86_64 (kernel 6.2.0-39-generic)
tradeoffs: Gains attributed to aggressive caching design; large (1000-key) range queries show only a marginal 1.11x edge, so the advantage narrows for big scans; single-machine, single-hardware-config benchmark
caveats: First-party benchmark (TidesDB's own blog and benchtool repo), not an independent third party; methodology (workload, versions, hardware) is fully stated so kept at A rather than downgraded to C, but should be treated as a vendor claim
found_via: HN Algolia search 'faster than RocksDB' -> 'TidesDB: 4.7x faster seeks than RocksDB via aggressive caching'

name: IBTree (Interpolating B-Tree, SOSD implementation)
workload: SOSD benchmark point lookups on the amzn dataset (200M 64-bit keys), best-configured variant of each structure, single-threaded
claimed_speedup: 446.55 ns vs BTree's 482.11 ns lookup latency (~8% faster, derived from page data) while using 9.0 MB vs BTree's 166.0 MB (~18x smaller)
compiler_and_flags: Clang, CMake Release build (-O3) with -march=native -ffast-math (per SOSD's CMakeLists.txt)
tradeoffs: Implements interpolation search inside B-tree nodes per G. Graefe's 2018 VLDB paper 'B-tree indexes, interpolation search, and skew'; only exists as a template competitor inside the SOSD benchmark harness, not a standalone packaged library; degrades on skewed/adversarial key distributions where interpolation mispredicts
caveats: Single dataset (amzn) and single size point reported in Table 2 of the Hist-Tree/CIDR'21 paper (which reuses SOSD); the win margin is modest (~8%) and the paper's main point is that CHT/PGM do even better; SOSD repo itself has had no commits since 2022
found_via: SOSD benchmark Table 1/competitors listing + Table 2 numbers quoted in the CIDR 2021 Hist-Tree paper

name: FAST (Fast Architecture Sensitive Tree, SOSD implementation)
workload: SOSD benchmark point lookups on the amzn dataset (200M 64-bit keys), best-configured variant of each structure, single-threaded
claimed_speedup: 435.33 ns vs BTree's 482.11 ns lookup latency (~10% faster, derived from page data) while using 102.0 MB vs BTree's 166.0 MB
compiler_and_flags: Clang, CMake Release build (-O3) with -march=native -ffast-math (per SOSD's CMakeLists.txt)
tradeoffs: Reimplementation of Kim et al.'s SIGMOD'10 SIMD-friendly cache-sensitive tree layout; only exists as a template competitor inside the SOSD benchmark harness, uses SSE2 intrinsics (emmintrin.h), 32-bit key path is separate from 64-bit; not a standalone maintained library
caveats: Single dataset (amzn) and single size point; original FAST paper claimed much larger GPU/SIMD speedups in its own (unavailable) benchmark, this is a smaller, independently reimplemented result from SOSD/CIDR'21; SOSD repo has had no commits since 2022
found_via: SOSD benchmark Table 1/competitors listing + Table 2 numbers quoted in the CIDR 2021 Hist-Tree paper
